record.paper_title: The Quest for Equational Axiomatizations of Parallel Composition: Status and Open Problems
record.original_question: Prove the stronger version of the non-finite-axiomatizability claim for observation congruence: for the recursion-, relabelling-, and restriction-free CCS language, the negative result should remain true after extending the language by any finite collection of GSOS operations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the process algebra CCS without recursion, relabelling, and restriction, whose signature consists of the constant 0 (inaction), a unary action prefix a._ for each action a drawn from a set including a distinguished silent action τ together with a set of visible actions closed under complementation, the binary alternative composition +, and the binary parallel composition |, with the standard operational semantics. Let ≈^c denote observation congruence (the largest congruence contained in weak bisimilarity).

A GSOS operation is an operation whose operational semantics is specified by a finite set of GSOS rules, i.e., rules of De Simone-style form in which premises only test the immediate transitions of the arguments and rule conclusions have a single target term built from the arguments and their derivatives, conforming to the standard GSOS rule format of Bloom, Istrail, and Meyer.

Prove the following: for every finite collection G of GSOS operations, the equational theory of observation congruence ≈^c over the language obtained by extending the above recursion-, relabelling-, and restriction-free fragment of CCS with the operations in G admits no finite, sound, and complete axiomatization (with or without auxiliary operators in G). That is, there exists no finite set E of equations over this extended signature such that, for all closed terms t, u of the extended language, E ⊢ t = u if and only if t ≈^c u.
artifact.status_search_result: The strengthened non-finite-axiomatizability claim for observation congruence over recursion-, relabelling-, and restriction-free CCS, robust under extension by any finite collection of GSOS operations, is listed as an open problem in surveys of the axiomatization of parallel composition. Related results (e.g., non-finite axiomatizability for strong bisimilarity in the presence of complementary actions, and reduction-based lifting techniques for extensions) have been established, but the full GSOS-robust statement for observation congruence remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Quest for Equational Axiomatizations of Parallel Composition: Status and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open research problems include proving that observation congruence has no finite equational axiomatization over the recursion, relabelling and restriction free version of CCS, and possibly for all extensions with any finite collection of GSOS operations.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in the survey on axiomatization of parallel composition.

status_evidence.title: Lifting non-finite axiomatizability results to extensions of process algebras
status_evidence.snippet: A general technique has been developed for obtaining non-finite axiomatizability results for behavioural congruences over process algebras based on reduction mappings.
status_evidence.claim: General lifting techniques exist for related non-finite axiomatizability results but do not settle the observation-congruence GSOS-robust case.

status_evidence.title: CCS with Hennessy's Merge has no Finite Equational Axiomatization
status_evidence.snippet: Impossible to provide a finite axiomatization of the recursion free fragment of CCS modulo bisimulation using Hennessy's merge operator.
status_evidence.claim: Related negative result for strong bisimilarity; the observation-congruence GSOS-extension version remains open.
